quizzes.title: Checkpoint 1 — Brand, Positioning, and Profile
quizzes.intro: Check whether you understand personal branding ethics, positioning, and core LinkedIn profile elements.

questions.prompt: What is a practical definition of personal brand in this course?

options.text: A costume you invent with no connection to your work
The reputation you intentionally steer through focus, proof, and consistent communication
A guarantee of viral fame
A substitute for building real skills

questions.explanation: Brand is steered reputation grounded in substance and clarity—not cosplay or hype.

wrongExplanations.c: Virality is not the goal or a promise.

options.text: I am a passionate synergistic professional.
I help small e-commerce teams understand weekly sales drivers through clear dashboards and SQL, as shown by cutting report prep dramatically.
I do everything for everyone online.
Hire me because I want opportunities.

questions.explanation: Strong positioning names audience, outcome, method, and proof.

wrongExplanations.c: Overly broad focus helps no stranger remember you.

questions.prompt: What should a LinkedIn headline often include beyond a bare job title?

options.text: Only emojis and ‘open to work’ with no specialty
Value, niche, or outcome signals a stranger can understand quickly
A full autobiography
Invented executive titles you do not hold

questions.explanation: Headlines work as skimmable value signals, not empty slogans or false ranks.

questions.prompt: Which About section approach fits the lesson?

options.text: First person, who you help, proof points, and a soft call to action
Third-person hype with no proof
A paste of your entire resume with no narrative
Confidential metrics you are not allowed to share

questions.explanation: About sections teach strangers quickly with proof and a next step.

options.text: Invent metrics if they sound impressive
Do not invent titles, employers, or credentials; long careers favor claims that survive scrutiny
Buy fake followers for social proof
Leak confidential roadmaps for engagement

questions.explanation: Trust compounds; fabricated claims and leaks destroy careers.

wrongExplanations.d: Confidential leaks are a serious mistake.

quizzes.title: Checkpoint 2 — Proof, Content, and Networking
quizzes.intro: Apply experience bullets, content habits, and respectful networking.

questions.prompt: Which experience bullet best matches the recommended pattern?

options.text: Responsible for various duties and passionate teamwork
Automated weekly inventory reconciliation in Python, cutting manual checks from 6 hours to 45 minutes
Worked on stuff with stakeholders
Helped with things as needed

questions.explanation: Action, scope, and result make bullets credible and skimmable.

questions.prompt: What kind of LinkedIn content does the course prefer?

options.text: Engagement bait demanding ‘comment YES’
Small honest lessons from real work that teach others
Posts claiming work you did not do
Confidential screenshots for clout

questions.explanation: Teaching from real experience beats bait, fakery, and leaks.

options.text: Hi, can we connect? I need a job.
A short note with context, why them, a specific small ask, and an easy out
A pasted novel sales pitch sent to hundreds identically
An immediate product dump right after connecting with no context

questions.explanation: Respectful, specific asks convert better and protect reputation.

wrongExplanations.d: Pitch-slapping after connect is a common mistake.

questions.prompt: What is a better brand health signal than raw likes alone?

options.text: Meaningful conversations, referrals, and opportunities aligned with your positioning
Only emoji reaction counts
Number of arguments won in comments
How often you post confidential drama

questions.explanation: Career-relevant responses matter more than vanity metrics.

questions.prompt: Why can thoughtful commenting build reputation efficiently?

options.text: Because saying only ‘Great post’ makes you memorable
Because adding experience, caveats, or resources shows expertise in context
Because comments replace the need for any proof on your profile
Because rude debates always attract recruiters

questions.explanation: Substantive comments demonstrate thinking where audiences already pay attention.

quizzes.title: Final Quiz — Systems, Boundaries, and Long Game
quizzes.intro: Use the full lesson. Focus on maintenance, ethics, boundaries, and sustainable brand systems.

questions.prompt: What is a sound weekly branding budget mindset?

options.text: Let branding consume all skill-building time
Small blocks for proof/content and thoughtful engagement so branding supports—not replaces—skill growth
Zero maintenance forever after one profile polish
Post constantly even with nothing useful to say

questions.explanation: Sustainable budgets keep substance first and communication consistent.

questions.prompt: How should career changers brand themselves?

options.text: Claim senior titles overnight
Translate transferable wins honestly and show learning proof without exaggeration
Hide all past experience as irrelevant
Invent metrics from thin air

questions.explanation: Bridge narratives with real transferable proof beat fake seniority.

questions.prompt: What should you do before posting employer-related details?

options.text: Assume everything internal is fair game
Respect policies; prefer generic lessons over confidential roadmaps; ask when unsure
Leak screenshots for authenticity points
Tag competitors with private pricing

questions.explanation: Personal brand should not require burning employer trust.

wrongExplanations.d: Sharing private pricing is harmful and unprofessional.

questions.prompt: Which statement about AI writing help is aligned with the course?

options.text: Publish generic AI posts unchanged as thought leadership
Use AI to edit structure or grammar while you supply facts and keep your voice
Let AI invent credentials
AI removes the need for proof artifacts

questions.explanation: AI is an assistant for clarity, not a source of fake substance.

questions.prompt: What belongs in a quarterly brand review?

options.text: Updating shareable proof, fixing dead links, checking tone, and weeding outdated posts
Buying reactions
Deleting all recommendations on principle
Switching identity claims weekly for fun

questions.explanation: Gardening the profile and content keeps the brand accurate and trustworthy.

questions.prompt: Which trio captures the course’s long-game advice?

options.text: Be findable, be believable, be kind under pressure
Be invisible, be exaggerated, be hostile in comments
Be viral, be vague, be always selling
Be secretive about all proof, be frantic, be inconsistent

questions.explanation: Findability, credibility, and professionalism compound better than hype tactics.

wrongExplanations.c: Virality and vagueness are weak strategies here.
